full_judgment:
6. Mr. A.K.M. Sha6qur Rahman, the Jearned Advocate appearing on behalf of the respondents has submitted that presumption of khtians loses its weight with the passage of time and that the entries in the subsequent khatian would be more acceptable to a court than the entree in the earlier khatian. According to him the latter Khatian should relatively have more weight than the previous one. He has further submitted that the presumption of the C.S. Khatian which is subsequent in point of time was rightly accepted by the courts below than those in the batwara khatian; according to him the C.S. khatian having been prepared subsequently in 1915-18 should prevail over the batwara khatian prepared in 1908 inasmuch that the earlier Batwara khatian must be deemed to have been considered and rejected. He has also submitted that the court of appeal below accepting the evidence of the witnesses of the P.Ws. has found that the plaintiffs’ predecessor Jamiruddin Mir possessed the suit land i.e. the lands of batwara khatain No. 38. 

 7. As regards the presumption of the C. S. Khatian upon which the courts below have held that the suit properties originally belonged to Arman Mir and Jamiruddin Mir, it appears that apart from the presumption of the C.S. Khatians, the trial court has elaborately considered the oral evidence of the witnesses of the plaintiff. Court of appeal below has considered the evidence of P.W. Wasuddin aged about 90 years. This witness has denied that Amiruddin Mir and Jamiruddin Mir came to this place from a southern country. He has deposed that Arman Mir and Jamiruddin Mir are the sons of Dhanai Mir. Other witnesses of the plaintiff have deposed that the suit lands were possessed by the heirs of Arman Mir and Jamiruddin Mir. The trial court has also considered the oral evidence of the witnesses for the defendants 

 10. In my view the presumption that was attached to the batwara khatian lost its relative weight after C S. Khatian came into being in 1915-18. In the absence of any other evidence the latter khatian was rightly accepted by the courts below in proof of the state of affairs existed at the time when the records were prepared and that the presumption of the C.S, Khatian in my view could not be rebutted by the defendants by any cogent evidences and the courts below correctly accepted the entries in the C.S. records. I am further of the opinion that the presumption of the C.S. Khatian did not lose its weight because of absence of evidence as to its basis (14 D.L.R. 725). It further appears that the trial court has also noticed the evidence of D.Ws. 7 and 8 who are heirs of Arman Mir. They have claimed their saham on the basis that the properties belonged to Arman Mir and Jamiruddin Mir. If they have supported the case of the defendants they could claim a double share than what they have claimed by an application for saham.
